extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians and computational algebraists needing library procedure reference)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR libraries (chern.lib, cimonom.lib, classify2.lib, classify_aeq.lib, classifyMapGerms.lib). For each procedure it lists usage, argument types, return type, purpose, notes and examples demonstrating expected behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: dualPart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dualPart( I [,N] ); I list of integers, N integer. Return: list of integers. Purpose: computes the partition dual (conjugate) to I. Note: the result is extended by zeroes to length N if an optional integer parameter N is given and the length of the computed dual partition is smaller than N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows LIB "chern.lib"; list I = 1,3,4; print( dualPart(I) ); Output: 1,2,2,3. Use N only to pad with zeros when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PartC
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PartC( I, m); I list of integers, m integer. Return: list of integers. Purpose: computes the complement of a partition with respect to m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: returns the zero partition if the maximal element of the partition is smaller than m. Example: Complement of (1,3,4) with respect to 5 gives 1,2,4.

rubrics_metrics.name: partOver
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: partOver( n, J); n integer, J list of integers (partition). Return: list of lists. Purpose: computes the partitions over a given one with summands not exceeding n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: partOver(4, 3,3,4) prints partitions over (3,3,4) with summands not exceeding 4. Output is a list of partitions (example output illustrated in manual).

rubrics_metrics.name: partUnder
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: partUnder(J); J list of integers (partition). Return: list of lists. Purpose: computes the partitions under a given one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: partUnder(0,1,1) lists partitions under (0,1,1). Example output is shown. No extra options documented for this procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: SegreA
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: SegreA(I); I an ideal. Return: list of integers. Purpose: computes the Segre classes of the subscheme defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In a 3-dimensional projective space, for ideal I=xy,xz,yz, SegreA(I) returns [0,0,3,...]. Other examples include coplanar and non-coplanar arrangements; inspect outputs for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FultonA
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: FultonA(I); I an ideal. Return: list of integers. Purpose: computes the Fulton classes of the subscheme defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For I=xy,xz,yz in P^3, FultonA(I) returns [0,0,3,2]. For other ideals, example outputs illustrate behavior. Uses same input style as SegreA.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSMA
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CSMA(I); I an ideal. Return: list of integers. Purpose: computes the Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of the variety defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For smooth cubic I=x^3+y^3+z^3 returns [0,3,0]; for singular cubics like xyz returns [0,3,3]; for x*y*(x+y) returns [0,3,4]. Shows different outputs depending on singularity type.

rubrics_metrics.name: EulerAff
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: EulerAff(I); I an ideal. Return: integer. Purpose: computes the Euler characteristic of the affine variety defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ring r = 0,(x,y), dp; ideal I = y2-x3-x-1; EulerAff(I) returns 3. Use for affine Euler characteristic computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EulerProj
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: EulerProj(I); I an ideal. Return: integer. Purpose: computes the highest degree term of the Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson class of the variety defined by I, which equals the Euler characteristic. Note: uses CSMA(...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For projective cubic ideals, EulerProj returns 3 in the given examples. Use when working in projective setting to obtain Euler characteristic.

rubrics_metrics.name: BelongSemig
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: BelongSemig (n,v[,sup]); n bigint, v and sup intvec. Return: In default form returns 1 if n is in the semigroup generated by elements of v or 0 otherwise. If sup is given and n belongs, returns a monomial in variables {x(i)|i in sup} of degree n with deg(x(sup[j])) = v[j]. Assume: v and sup positive integer vectors of same size, sup has no repeated entries, x(i) must be an indeterminate in current ring for all i in sup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: LIB "cimonom.lib"; ring r=0,x(1..5),dp; BelongSemig(125, 13,17,51, sup=2,4,1) returns x(2)^7*x(4)^2; BelongSemig(125,v) returns 1. Use sup to get constructive monomial when membership holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: MinMult
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: MinMult (a, b); a integer, b integer vector. Return: an integer k, the minimum positive integer such that k*a belongs to the semigroup generated by integers in b. Assume: a positive integer, b positive integer vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: MinMult(46, [13,17,59]) returns 3, with comment showing decomposition (3*a = 8*b[1] + 2*b[2]). Use to find minimal multiplier to place number into semigroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompInt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CompInt(d); d intvec. Return: 1 if the toric ideal I(d) is a complete intersection or 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: if printlevel > 0, additional info is displayed; printlevel >=1 shows a minimal set of generators (quasihomogeneous binomials); printlevel >=2 and gcd(d)=1 also shows Frobenius number. Examples show outputs and generator lists when printlevel increased.

rubrics_metrics.name: complexClassify
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: complexClassify(f); f Poly. Assume: f is a bivariate polynomial defining a curve singularity at (0,0) of modality <=2 and corank <=2; ordering of base ring must be local. Return: A normal form equation g for f represented by an element of type NormalFormEquation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: final scaling step not implemented; may need rescaling x->lambda1*x, y->lambda2*y. Case X9 not implemented (returns error). Access normal form via g.normalFormEquation.value after setting ring. Example demonstrates calling complexClassify on a large polynomial and reading properties (Corank, Normalform equation type, Milnor number, Modality, Determinacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: complexType
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: complexType(f); f Poly. Assume: f is a bivariate polynomial defining a curve singularity at (0,0) of modality and corank <=2; ordering of basering must be local. Return: A list with the complex type of f and the modality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: complexType(f) returns entries indicating type (e.g., Y[8,7]) and modality (e.g., 1). Use to get classification label and modality.

rubrics_metrics.name: sagbiAlg
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from classify_aeq.lib. Return: An ideal containing the sagbi bases of I. (Usage shown with ring and ideal inputs.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: LIB "classify_aeq.lib"; ring R=0,t,ds; ideal I=...; sagbiAlg(I); outputs a list of generators (sagbi basis) and additional relations. Use to compute sagbi bases of subalgebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: sagbiMod
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from classify_aeq.lib. Return: An ideal: the sagbi bases for the differential module. (Examples show output generators.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage computes sagbi basis for the module derived from given generators via diff(G,t). Output lists basis elements. Useful for module-level sagbi computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: semiGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from classify_aeq.lib. Return: list L with three entries associated to the algebra generated by the sagbi basis: generators of the semigroup, the conductor, the semigroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: semiGroup(I) returns entries like [1]: 8,10,12,23,27; [2]: 30; [3]: list of semigroup elements. Use to extract semigroup data (generators, conductor, full semigroup).

rubrics_metrics.name: semiMod
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from classify_aeq.lib. Return: list K where K[1] min generators of semialgebra; K[2] conductor of algebra; K[3] generators for semialgebra; K[4] min generators of module; K[5] conductor of module; K[6] semigroup of the module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example outputs demonstrate the six components (generators, conductors, semigroups). Use for combined semialgebra and semimodule data.

rubrics_metrics.name: planeCur
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from classify_aeq.lib. Return: An ideal. Purpose: Ideal is one of the singularities in the list of Bruce and Gaffney. (Usage: supply ideal from parametrization; returns identifying ideal.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: planeCur(I) on a long series returns an ideal indicating which normal form matches. Use to test if given parametrization corresponds to known normal forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: spaceCur
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from classify_aeq.lib. Return: an ideal. Purpose: Ideal is one of the singularities in the list of C.G. Gibson and C.A. Hobbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: spaceCur(I) returns small ideals indicating the matched normal form. Use for space curve classification against reference lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHnormalForm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: HHnormalForm(I), I = <x(t),y(t)> an ideal, optional # bound for the conductor. Compute: computes the Hefez-Hernandez normal form of the ideal I=<x(t),y(t)>. Return: a list L with 5 entries: L[1] Hefez-Hernandez normal form of I, L[2] the semigroup Gamma, L[3] the semimodule Lambda, L[4] 0 if Lambda=Gamma or lambda=min(Lambda-Gamma)-n (the Zariski number), L[5] integers i>lambda with i+n not in Lambda or 0 if empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: HHnormalForm(I) returns components including normal form power series and semigroup/module lists. Use when computing analytic invariants and normal forms for plane branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: modSagbiAlg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modSagbiAlg(I,i); I an ideal, i an integer (optional). Return: ideal, a sagbi basis for I using modular methods. Purpose: computes a sagbi basis using modular techniques. If second argument is 0 then the result is not verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: modSagbiAlg(I,0) and modSagbiAlg(I) show identical outputs in examples. Use modular variant for performance and optional verification control.

rubrics_metrics.name: coDimMap
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: coDimMap(I, #); I=ideal, #=list. Compute: a bound of the A-determinacy of the map germ defined by I. Return: a list where 1st entry gives bound of A-determinacy and 2nd entry gives the codimension of the map germ defined by I. Note: if # is empty it computes A^e-codimension (the extended codimension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: coDimMap(I) returns [14,2]; coDimMap(I,1) returns [15,4]. Use to obtain determinacy bounds and codimension for map-germ classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: coDim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: coDim(module M, module N, ideal I, int bound, list #); M is a submodule in A^r over basering A, N is a submodule in R^r over subring R generated by entries of I. Compute: computes the K-vector space dimension of A^r / (M + N + maxideal(bound)*A^r). Return: an integer. Note: if # is not empty the bound is corrected by computing determinacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates formation of M,N from jacob(I) and uses coDim(M,N,I,15) returning numeric codimension (example returned 6). Use for linear algebraic codimension/dimension calculations in classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: vStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vStd(M, N, I, bound); M submodule in A^r over basering A, N a submodule in R^r over subring R generated by entries of I. Compute: a standard basis of M+N+maxideal(bound)*A^r. Return: a list whose 1st entry gives a list where each entry is a generator of the standard basis and 2nd entry gives a list of generators after reduced echelon form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: vStd(M,N,I,15) produces multi-component lists with explicit generators (large expressions printed). Use to compute standard bases for module sums and view reduced echelon generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: modVStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modVStd(M, N, I, bound, #); M submodule in A^r, N submodule in R^r, I ideal, bound integer, optional #. Compute: a standard basis of A^r / (M+N+maxideal(bound)*A^r) using modular methods. Return: a list whose 1st entry gives list of generators of standard basis and 2nd entry gives reduced echelon form generators. Note: if # is not empty the bound is corrected by computing determinacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the modular version of vStd for performance; examples are invoked similarly in the classifyMapGerms.lib context. Use when modular acceleration and verification behavior is desired.
